cards.front: What are the three types of plate boundaries? Give one example of each.
cards.back: Divergent (Mid-Atlantic Ridge), Convergent (Himalayas — India-Eurasia collision), Transform (San Andreas Fault). Earthquakes occur at all three; volcanism mainly at divergent/convergent.

cards.front: Name the major passes connecting India: Nathu La, Shipki La, Zoji La — with their states.
cards.back: Nathu La — Sikkim (to Tibet); Shipki La — Himachal Pradesh (Sutlej enters India); Zoji La — Ladakh/Kashmir (Srinagar–Leh, on NH-1).

cards.front: What is the difference between El Niño and La Niña, and their effect on the Indian monsoon?
cards.back: El Niño: warming of central/eastern Pacific → generally weakens the Indian monsoon (drought risk). La Niña: cooling of the same region → generally strengthens the monsoon.

cards.front: Which rivers form the following: Jog Falls, Dhuandhar Falls, Shivanasamudra Falls?
cards.back: Jog (Gerosoppa) Falls — Sharavati (Karnataka); Dhuandhar — Narmada (Bhedaghat, MP); Shivanasamudra — Kaveri (Karnataka, one of India's first hydroelectric stations, 1902).

cards.front: Which straits separate: (a) India–Sri Lanka, (b) Malaysia–Indonesia, (c) Spain–Morocco?
cards.back: (a) Palk Strait (b) Strait of Malacca (c) Strait of Gibraltar. Palk Strait connects Palk Bay with the Bay of Bengal.
Weathering: in-situ breakdown of rocks (physical/chemical/biological), no movement. Erosion: wearing away AND transport of material by agents (rivers, wind, glaciers, waves).

cards.front: What are laterite soils, where are they found in India, and which crops suit them?
cards.back: Formed by intense leaching in high-rainfall tropical areas; rich in iron/aluminium oxides, poor in nitrogen & lime. Found: Western Ghats, Odisha, parts of NE. Crops: tea, coffee, cashew, tapioca (with manuring).

cards.front: What is a temperature inversion and when does it commonly occur?
cards.back: When temperature increases with altitude (reversal of normal lapse rate). Common on calm, clear, long winter nights over valleys — traps pollutants and causes fog/frost pockets.

cards.front: Which is the only large river of peninsular India that flows through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea (besides Tapi)?
cards.back: Narmada — flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, forming an estuary (not a delta). Tapi follows a parallel rift to its south.

cards.front: Name the grasslands: North America, South America, Africa, Central Asia, Australia.
cards.back: Prairies (N. America), Pampas (S. America), Savanna/Veld (Africa; Veld in S. Africa), Steppes (Central Asia/Eurasia), Downs (Australia).
